sources.note: Bootstraps a model's reasoning ability from a handful of rationale examples by generating rationales, keeping only those that reach the right answer, and finetuning on them in a loop.
sources.title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning

sources.note: Generalizes chain-of-thought into a search over a tree of intermediate 'thoughts', letting a model self-evaluate branches, look ahead and backtrack instead of committing to one left-to-right path.
sources.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models

sources.note: Synthesizes Cognitive Behavioral Therapy dialogues using a CoT strategy grounded in CBT guidelines plus a resistance orchestrator that steers simulated patients away from sycophantic compliance.
sources.title: ODRA: Synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions with Structured Chain-Of-Thought and Dynamic Patient Resistance

sources.note: An Italian proverb benchmark on which models complete proverbs successfully but fail multiple-choice selection when no correct option is present, with CoT analysis showing they name the right ending while failing to notice its absence.
sources.title: Easy to Complete, Hard to Choose: Investigating LLM Performance on the ProverbIT Benchmark

sources.note: A training-free two-stage prompting protocol that extracts a problem's answer-space constraints first and then checks its own intermediate and final results against them, routed on by a regex detector.
sources.title: Constraint-First Reasoning: A Training-Free Protocol for Exploiting Answer-Space Constraints in Mathematical Problem Solving

sources.note: A trustworthiness benchmark for reasoning models over truthfulness, safety and efficiency, using training paradigm as an analytical axis, and finding reasoning models more fragile than plain LLMs to reasoning-induced risks.
sources.title: Red Teaming Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Reframes unlearning in reasoning models as an intervention on the CoT itself, having the model generate logically valid counterfactual traces and iteratively preference-tuning toward them.
sources.title: CiPO: Counterfactual Unlearning for Large Reasoning Models through Iterative Preference Optimization

sources.note: Identifies a multimodal failure where models see the risky visual cue but let narrative coherence override safety as reasoning proceeds, and defends against it by extracting intent before generation.
sources.title: Mitigating Safety Context Amnesia in Multimodal Reasoning Models via Intent-Guided Safety Reasoning

sources.note: Switches to soft-embedding latent reasoning only at low-confidence steps, keeping discrete decoding elsewhere, and pushes the soft embeddings away from the top token to stop them collapsing.
sources.title: SeLaR: Selective Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

sources.note: Reformulates reasoning as a search over thinking strategies, showing sparse reasoning paths exist that are simultaneously more accurate and shorter than standard outputs.
sources.title: Neural Chain-of-Thought Search: Searching the Optimal Reasoning Path to Enhance Large Language Models

sources.note: Derives a non-vacuous PAC-Bayes generalization bound for transformers on boolean functions in terms of Fourier sparsity and degree, and uses it to show chain of thought turns an exponential dependence on reasoning length into a linear one for Parity.
sources.title: A Sharper Picture of Generalization in Transformers

sources.note: Defines certaindex, an algorithm-agnostic measure of how much a reasoning algorithm's answer has stopped changing, and builds it into a serving system that reallocates or terminates compute per query — saving up to 50% of tokens in batch inference and tripling online throughput.
sources.title: Efficiently Scaling LLM Reasoning with Certaindex

sources.note: Characterizes exactly how much computational power a chain of thought buys as a function of its length, sandwiching the class of languages a decoder recognizes with t(n) decoding steps between two standard complexity classes.
sources.title: The Expressive Power of Transformers with Chain of Thought

sources.note: Turns each intermediate step of a reasoning trajectory into a numerical feature vector of distances to the answer choices, projects those into 2D to visualize how trajectories move through answer space, and reuses the same features to build a lightweight verifier for weighted voting.
sources.title: Landscape of Thoughts: Visualizing the Reasoning Process of Large Language Models

sources.note: Pins down the VC dimension of transformers as depth times parameters times a logarithm, and shows chain-of-thought learning by teacher forcing costs only logarithmically more as the number of reasoning steps grows.
sources.title: Tight Sample Complexity of Transformers

sources.note: Explains why latent chain-of-thought excels at exploration but fails at computation by identifying decisional certainty as the governing variable, formalizing it as the Symbolic Index, and proving that curriculum learning is not merely helpful but necessary for training latent reasoners.
sources.title: Capabilities and Fundamental Limits of Latent Chain-of-Thought

sources.note: Replaces uniform test-time compute allocation with a training-free agent that picks reasoning tools, a search strategy and an exploration parameter per problem, using a process reward model both to prune within a trajectory and to select across iterations.
sources.title: What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?

sources.note: Proves a tighter no-CoT upper bound of AC^0 for constant-precision transformers, and shows T steps of chain of thought let a constant-depth model compute anything a size-T boolean circuit can.
sources.title: Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems

sources.note: Proves that reasoning can be moved from emitted tokens into hidden states without losing sample efficiency, using a curriculum that deletes thinking tokens in geometric chunks and so needs only logarithmically many training stages.
sources.title: Transformers Provably Learn to Internalize Chain-of-Thought

sources.note: Gives the first optimization guarantee that gradient descent trains constant-depth transformers to solve NC1-complete problems with chain of thought, and shows the algebraic structure of the task decides how far the learned reasoning extrapolates.
sources.title: Transformers Provably Learn Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Length Generalization

result.definition: Emitting intermediate tokens before an answer, and the object almost everything in this archive is about — now with a theoretical account of why it works. Twenty sources use it in three distinct roles. As a computational device: each emitted token re-enters the input, so generation raises usable depth, and the archived complexity results characterize exactly what that buys — logarithmic steps add essentially nothing, linear steps allow simulating recurrence and all regular languages, polynomial steps reach exactly P. As a learning device: CoT changes Parity's generalization bound from exponential to linear in reasoning length, and costs only logarithmically more in sample complexity, so long chains are statistically cheap. As a readable artefact: monitors, faithfulness probes and unlearning interventions all read or edit the trace, and it is here that the archive's evidence is least comfortable — traces causally shape outputs while models decline to report that influence. The three roles come apart, which is why a claim that CoT 'helps' has to say which one it means.
